brief.heading: Where the 2026 path stands
brief.body: The House-passed HJR 203 path is blocked because the proposal died in Senate Appropriations. Official Florida Senate bill pages reviewed on June 2, 2026 list CS/HJR 1-F as ordered enrolled, while CS/SJR 2-F was laid on the table and referred to CS/HJR 1-F. Official Florida Senate bill pages reviewed on June 2, 2026 list CS/SB 4-F as ordered enrolled, while CS/HB 3-F was laid on the table and referred to CS/SB 4-F.

status_legend.label: Red
status_legend.meaning: Blocked, dead, or not currently moving

months.title: House vehicle filed
months.summary: HJR 203 entered the 2026 regular-session bill record.

months.title: House passed; Senate received

months.title: No Special Session D vehicle found
months.summary: The reviewed bill-actions list did not show a tracked property-tax elimination proposal.

months.title: Special Session 2026-F bills wait for June 1 agenda
months.summary: Official Senate bill pages list SJR 2-F and SB 4-F on the June 1 Appropriations committee agenda; the May 31 bill-actions page reported no bill actions.

months.title: Special Session 2026-F final floor actions posted
months.summary: Bill actions and bill pages for June 2, 2026 show CS/HJR 1-F and CS/SB 4-F were ordered enrolled, while CS/SJR 2-F and CS/HB 3-F were laid on the table in favor of those advancing vehicles.

months.title: Watch for additional filings and committee movement
months.summary: Additional special-session bills, new regular-session filings, or committee agendas would need official source support before this tracker marks a vehicle moving beyond filing.

months.title: Ballot and voter approval checkpoints
months.summary: A constitutional-amendment path would still require voter approval before any constitutional change.

path_steps.label: Filed
path_steps.title: HJR 203 entered the House record
path_steps.description: The House property-tax proposal that became CS/CS/HJR 203 was filed for the 2026 regular session.
path_steps.dependency: This created the primary House vehicle tracked in the elimination debate.

path_steps.label: House
path_steps.title: House approval completed
path_steps.description: CS/CS/HJR 203 passed the Florida House by an 80-30 vote.
path_steps.dependency: A legislative constitutional amendment also needed Senate approval before any ballot step.

path_steps.label: Senate
path_steps.title: Senate path blocked
path_steps.description: CS/CS/HJR 203 died in Senate Appropriations.
path_steps.dependency: This ended the regular-session path for that specific House proposal.

path_steps.label: Floor
path_steps.title: House substitute advanced; SB 4-F enrolled
path_steps.description: The June 2, 2026 bill-actions page and official bill pages show CS/HJR 1-F and CS/SB 4-F were ordered enrolled, while CS/SJR 2-F and CS/HB 3-F were laid on the table in favor of those vehicles.
path_steps.dependency: The next public checkpoints move beyond floor action to enrolled text, ballot records, and any Governor action on SB 4-F.

path_steps.label: Ballot
path_steps.title: Ballot listing not reached
path_steps.description: A legislative constitutional amendment would still need voter approval before it could change the Florida Constitution.
path_steps.dependency: The Department of State ballot step comes after a measure advances through the required constitutional-amendment path.

next_panels.label: What changed
next_panels.body: On June 2, 2026, the Senate bill page showed CS/SJR 2-F was laid on the table in favor of CS/HJR 1-F, which was ordered enrolled.

next_panels.label: What to watch
next_panels.body: Watch enrolled text, any Governor action on SB 4-F, and whether the Department of State posts a ballot record for the advancing joint resolution.

next_panels.label: Data depth
next_panels.body: Pre-meeting analyses say the Revenue Estimating Conference had not reviewed SJR 2-F or SB 4-F; keep county comparisons separate until version-labeled estimates exist.

known_unknowns: Governor action on SB 4-F remains a watch checkpoint.
A Department of State ballot record remains a watch checkpoint if the advancing joint resolution completes the constitutional-amendment path.
County-impact comparisons need version-labeled sources before they should be treated as comparable.
